MEASURED BASIS 07-24: 51 live CloudWatch alarms with NO semantic census -- the alarm surface is the only estate capability with no product-grouped view, which is how bad denominators happen when scanning it. DELIVERABLE #1: alarm-map.json -- the exact twin of trigger-map.json (per-alarm: unit, tf_file, metric, threshold, actions, ENABLED/disabled, orphan-vs-TF-managed), plus an alarm-census.py and the same CI drift gate the trigger twin already has. THEN: the cleanup axis -- orphaned alarms (alarming on deleted resources), alarms whose SNS targets are dead, duplicates -- as RETIREMENT candidates routed through normal decommission discipline. MORATORIUM COMPLIANCE, STATED AT REGISTRATION SO IT CANNOT DRIFT: Andrew's standing moratorium (CLAUDE.md, 07-28: no new alarms/SNS/SES/monitors unless he explicitly asks) GOVERNS this project. This project is a CENSUS AND CLEANUP of what already exists -- it documents and RETIRES; it never creates. Any finding of a 'missing' alarm is recorded as a finding and STOPS there; building it requires Andrew's explicit word per the moratorium.

hazards: SCOPE INVERSION is the failure mode this registration text exists to prevent: an agent reading 'OPAL_ALERTS' as a mandate to BUILD alerting. The moratorium governs; this project only documents and retires. The name is inherited from Andrew's 07-24 ask; the scope is the census.
An alarm retired without checking its ACTIONS chain may silently orphan an SNS topic or a downstream automation -- retirement candidates carry their action-target census before any destroy.
